earlier_instruction: +10 kg matches the signed change in water inventory. Using the worked example’s method, 20 kg enters and 10 kg leaves in five minutes. Subtracting the outflow from the inflow gives +10 kg. The 30 kg starting inventory is needed only if you want the final inventory. If you’d like to work on explaining this calculation in writing, share a draft passage and tell me what you want it to help its reader understand.

For the tank’s inventory, count water entering as positive and water leaving as negative, just as in the worked example. Over five minutes, 20 kg enters and 10 kg leaves, so the tank gains 10 kg. The plus sign in +10 kg expresses that gain. Your −10 kg compares the supply’s loss with the drain’s gain, which answers a different question. You’ve identified signed inventory changes as a topic to practice. Before we set a writing goal, share a sentence explaining your sign choice and tell me what you want a reader to understand from it.

packet.new_task: Two covered basins together contain 25 kg of water at the start of an interval. The delivery log records 2 kg entering from outside. A maintenance log records 11 kg moved from the west basin to the east basin. An outlet collects 8 kg outside the pair. These are all water movements. For one boundary enclosing both basins, report the signed change in total inventory over the interval. Enter a signed whole number followed by kg.

response.response: Yes, signed inventory changes are what I want to practice. I used “11 kg moved from the west basin to the east basin.” Both basins are inside my boundary, so I think that move doesn't change their total. I hesitated over whose loss I was counting, but for the pair, 2 kg comes in and 8 kg goes out. I picked minus because the pair ends up with less water. My answer is −6 kg.
